introduction: “The spirit of all deeds is the good-pleasure of God.” The guide begins with ascetics whose austerities gained them nothing, moves to the claim that the worth of every act depends on God’s acceptance, spends its long middle on grace, “neither the candle nor the lamp can be lighted through their own unaided efforts”, and ends with contentment and with paradise understood as God’s good pleasure itself. It closes by quoting Ephesians, and Christian theology has argued over this ground for most of its history. Paul is here on both sides of his own sentence: “work out your own salvation … for it is God which worketh in you”. Augustine’s prayer “Give what You command” is here, and James’s retort that faith without works is dead. The prophets’ preference for mercy over sacrifice matches the opening reading; the Qur’an says that acceptance from God is greater than the gardens; and Rábi‘a’s prayer to be shut out of Paradise if she worshipped for its sake says what reading 58 says. The hard question, raised by Paul’s own imagined objector, is why a God who gives grace to whom He will still finds fault.
questions: The readings say that deeds without God’s good pleasure are “lifeless”. How would a person know whether a deed has it? What tests do Micah, Hosea and Isaiah offer?

“Work out your own salvation … for it is God which worketh in you.” How do the readings divide the labour between effort and grace? Compare the saying “if he comes to Me walking, I go to him running”.
“He singleth out for His mercy whomsoever He willeth.” Paul hears the objection, “Why doth he yet find fault?” What in the readings (for instance 35 and 37) bears on it?
James says, “shew me thy faith without thy works”. Reading 62 names both faith and deeds. Is there a real disagreement among these texts, or a difference of emphasis?
Rábi‘a wanted neither Paradise nor escape from Hell, only God. Reading 58 says paradise is His good pleasure. What changes in a religious life when reward is understood this way?

outside.why: Austerities in the climes of India, the lawful denied, and nothing gained. The Qur’an of Christian monks: monasticism they invented; We ordained it not for them; only seeking Allah’s pleasure, and they observed it not with right observance.
Paul on rules of touch not, taste not, handle not: which things have a shew of wisdom in will worship, and humility, and neglecting of the body.
Though I bestow all my goods to feed the poor, and though I give my body to be burned, and have not charity, it profiteth me nothing.
God’s good pleasure and that of His servants named together. What doth the Lord require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God?
Every soul should consider where God’s good pleasure resides. Hosea’s answer: I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.
His good pleasure is not attained except through what He hath commanded. Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.
Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father.
What lasts is God’s good pleasure and conduct in accord with the teachings. Present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service.
Great and small affairs alike conformed to His good pleasure. George Herbert: teach me, my God and King, in all things Thee to see, and what I do in anything to do it as for Thee.
Whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men.
They have no desire except the good pleasure of God. The Qur’an: of mankind is he who would sell himself, seeking the pleasure of Allah.
All virtuous deeds, yet God not pleased, and they profit nothing. Without faith it is impossible to please him.

Deeds without the fragrance of His good pleasure are lifeless. Isaiah, of a fast God did not accept: is not this the fast that I have chosen? to loose the bands of wickedness, to deal thy bread to the hungry.
The whole universe is but a handful of clay in His grasp. The Qur’an: the whole earth is His handful on the Day of Resurrection.

Should God regard the one who broke the fast as one who kept it. Two men went up to pray; the one who fasted twice in the week and said so went home less justified than the one who said, God be merciful to me a sinner.

The reading and those after it hold that works without acceptance are nothing. James presses from the other side: faith, if it hath not works, is dead; shew me thy faith without thy works, and I will shew thee my faith by my works. Do the readings disagree with him?
Who hath cried after Thee and not been answered? The Lord is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart.
Neither candle nor lamp lights itself. I am the vine, ye are the branches: without me ye can do nothing.
Augustine’s one-line prayer, which began a long controversy about grace: give what You command, and command what You will.
A broken-winged bird that would soar. My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness.

No one is freed from selfish desires save by the Spirit’s confirming grace. Paul holds effort and grace in one sentence: work out your own salvation with fear and trembling, for it is God which worketh in you both to will and to do of his good pleasure. Which half do the readings stress?
Faith is a token of grace and not the result of justice. So then it is not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth, but of God that sheweth mercy.
The reading quotes this verse: for many are called, but few are chosen.
A life spent in worship and mortification, and the Kingdom not gained. When ye shall have done all those things which are commanded you, say, We are unprofitable servants.
“He singleth out for His mercy whomsoever He willeth.” The reading’s words are the Qur’an’s: such is the bounty of Allah, which He bestoweth upon whom He will.

Whom Thou willest Thou causest to draw nigh. Paul states the doctrine and then the protest: he hath mercy on whom he will; thou wilt say then, Why doth he yet find fault? Paul silences the question. Do the readings answer it, and how?
The reality of every great man proceeds from God. By the grace of God I am what I am.
Truth is unattainable except through the favour of the Spirit. The wind bloweth where it listeth: so is every one that is born of the Spirit.
God opens to every person a door of opportunity; some take it. A saying Muslims hold sacred makes grace answer the smallest effort many times over: if he comes to Me walking, I go to him running.
Francis Thompson imagines grace that will not wait to be sought: I fled Him, down the nights and down the days. Is grace in the readings offered, or does it pursue?
Withhold not from yourselves the grace of God. O taste and see that the Lord is good.
“Look not upon my hopes and my doings.” The publican would not lift up so much as his eyes unto heaven.
Ask of Him alone. Seek ye first the kingdom of God, and all these things shall be added unto you.
The friend’s part is contentment with the Friend’s good pleasure, even in separation. Not my will, but thine, be done.
Content with the will of God. Milton, blind and unable to work as he wished: God doth not need either man’s work or his own gifts; they also serve who only stand and wait.
One word of His good pleasure is better than all that is on earth. The word the servant hopes to hear: well done, thou good and faithful servant.
To be approved of God alone should be one’s aim. A voice from heaven: this is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.
To attain His good pleasure before the soul departs, were it for a moment. Fear not, little flock; for it is your Father’s good pleasure to give you the kingdom.
Paradise is first and foremost the good pleasure of God. The Qur’an, having promised gardens: and, greater far, acceptance from Allah. That is the supreme triumph.
Paradise in this life is His good pleasure. Allah hath pleasure in them and they have pleasure in Him.
Paradise is recognition, hellfire separation. Rábi‘a of Basra prayed to be burned in Hell if she worshipped from fear of it, and shut out of Paradise if from hope of it: Thou art enough for me.
The kingdom of God cometh not with observation: behold, the kingdom of God is within you.
Heaven depends on faith and on good deeds. As the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also.
The reading is this verse in a modern version. The King James: for by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: not of works, lest any man should boast.
The soul should work to purify itself, that it may merit God’s care. Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us.

shortfall: Readings 4 to 11 and 43 to 56 say in many forms that God’s good pleasure is the aim of every deed, and readings 25 to 34 that human gifts come by the Spirit; one or two companions answer each group, and the short prayers were left alone.

quran-pleasure-in-them.text: Their reward is with their Lord: Gardens of Eden underneath which rivers flow, wherein they dwell for ever. Allah hath pleasure in them and they have pleasure in Him. This is (in store) for him who feareth his Lord.
